$comment: Best-effort revenue estimates from PA budget office, IFO analyses, and prior gubernatorial proposals. All numbers are mid-range; treat as informative, not precise. Real revenue depends on tax rate, implementation, ramp-up, and economic conditions. Sources cited per row. Deficit updated to IFO's post-enactment FY 2026-27 General Fund Budget Update (July 2026), via Commonwealth Foundation. Refreshed November 2026 from IFO February 2026 Analysis of Revenue Proposals, PA Dept of Revenue February 2026 fiscal analyses, Gov. Shapiro FY 2026-27 Executive Budget, and IFO July 2026 enacted-budget General Fund analysis. Note: IFO November 2026 Five-Year Outlook not yet published as of refresh date (Nov 15).

proposals.name: Tax recreational cannabis
proposals.description: Pennsylvania is one of the few states without legal recreational cannabis. Gov. Shapiro's FY 2026-27 budget estimates $729M in year-one revenue from taxes and one-time licensing fees; the IFO puts mature recurring yield lower as license fees drop off.
proposals.statusDetail: HB 1200 passed PA House (May 2025) for the first time ever; killed in Senate; excluded from FY 2026-27 enacted budget
proposals.sourceDetail: IFO February 2026 Analysis of Revenue Proposals (mature recurring ~$432M, year-1 ~$140M); Shapiro FY 2026-27 executive budget ($729M year-1 including one-time license fees)

proposals.name: Tax skill games
proposals.description: The slot-like "skill game" terminals in PA bars and convenience stores operate in a legal gray area with no state tax. Shapiro proposed a 52% tax rate in FY 2026-27, projecting ~$766M in year-one revenue; industry estimates are lower.
proposals.statusDetail: PA Supreme Court declared skill games illegal (June 2026); enforcement deadline passed Oct 2026; multiple bills to regulate and tax introduced but no law enacted
proposals.sourceDetail: IFO February 2026 Analysis of Revenue Proposals (year-1 ~$487M, mature ~$1.19B at 52% rate); PA Supreme Court ruling Commonwealth v. Dent (June 2026)

proposals.name: Severance tax on natural gas
proposals.description: Pennsylvania is the only major natural gas–producing state without a traditional severance tax. We collect an "impact fee" instead, which brings in roughly a quarter of what a 5% severance tax would. The creative version: pair it with a faster corporate tax cut so it's a deal, not just a grab.
proposals.statusDetail: SB910 (6.5% rate) and HB2129 (9% base + export tax) introduced in 2025-2026 session; both stalled; industry lobby continues to block
proposals.sourceDetail: Prior Wolf-era budget proposals; PA Dept of Revenue analyses; SB910 and HB2129 (2025-2026 session); IFO impact fee revenue report (2025 fees: $243.9M)

proposals.name: Broaden sales tax to services & digital
proposals.description: PA's 6% sales tax applies to goods but exempts most services and the digital economy — subscriptions, streaming, consulting, SaaS. The tax code was designed for a 1970s goods economy. Broadening the base (even while modestly cutting the rate) generates billions in recurring revenue that grows with the modern economy rather than against it.
proposals.statusDetail: No active bill; politically heavy — would require broad legislative coalition
proposals.sourceDetail: PA IFO tax structure analyses; peer-state service-tax models (OH, MD, DC)

proposals.name: End the data center tax exemption
proposals.description: Act 7 of 2017 (expanded by HB 952 in 2022) waives the 6% PA sales tax on data center equipment — a corporate giveaway that has grown significantly as Amazon ($20B Salem Township), Microsoft (Three Mile Island), and others build major facilities here. Repeal or sunset the exemption rather than give away the boom.
proposals.statusDetail: HB 2198 (repeal) passed House 197-5; Senate passed similar language in HB 1667 44-6; both excluded from FY 2026-27 enacted budget signed July 12
proposals.sourceDetail: PA Dept of Revenue February 2026 fiscal analysis (FY 2026 cost: $188.4M, projected $517M/yr by 2030); HB 2198; HB 1667

proposals.name: Close the "Delaware loophole"
proposals.description: Combined corporate reporting — used by roughly half of US states — prevents multi-state corporations from shifting profits to no-tax-state subsidiaries to avoid PA corporate tax.
proposals.statusDetail: HB 1610 passed PA House 104-99 in June 2025; stalled in Republican-controlled Senate Finance Committee
proposals.sourceDetail: Gov. Shapiro FY 2026-27 budget ($328.4M FY 2026-27 projection); PA Policy Center April 2026 Revenue & Tax Fairness analysis; HB 1610 (2025-2026 session)

proposals.name: Industrial power consumption surcharge
proposals.description: A per-MWh surcharge on industrial-scale power consumers (data centers, crypto mining, large industrial loads). Targets facilities that strain the PJM grid and drive up rates for residential customers — without raising bills for ordinary Pennsylvanians.
proposals.statusDetail: Pre-bill stage; PA House passed HB 1834 (data center grid-cost protection bill, not a revenue surcharge) March 2026; per-MWh revenue surcharge concept still developing
proposals.sourceDetail: PA House HB 1834 (passed March 2026); PA PUC data center tariff proceedings (2026); ratepayer-advocate research
